newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks to revoke citizenship of accused Nazi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks to revoke citizenship of accused Nazi.

text.p: The Justice Department said on Tuesday it sued to revoke the U.S. citizenship of an accused member of the Nazi-backed Lithuanian security police who took part in persecuting Jews during the Second World War.

It filed a lawsuit in federal court in Florida alleging that Adolph Milius, a retired physician from St. Petersburg Beach, had been a member of the Lithuanian Security Police during the summer and autumn of 1941.
The security police assisted the occupying Nazi forces by arresting, detaining and turning over for execution or other punishment Jews in Vilnius Province.

The Justice Department's Nazi-hunting Office of Special Investigations said original wartime records cited in the lawsuit showed Milius, 78, participated in arresting Jews who were seeking to escape from the ghettos.
Department officials said he concealed his wartime activities when he came to the United States in 1949 and became a citizen six years later.
